blocks.text: In verses 8–16, “my servant” explicitly identifies Jacob, or Israel, and the address moves between singular and plural language. This makes it important not to assume that every use of servant language in Isaiah refers to one individual. Other singular servant passages have received differing identifications, including collective, prophetic, royal, and messianic readings; the language itself does not settle every question.

For the wider book of Isaiah, the Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters. It broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition while also containing thousands of spelling and substantive differences. Other Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings from Qumran likewise show that the book was transmitted and interpreted actively.
